([[Manhasset, New York]]) * [[The Patrick School]]
([[Hillside, New Jersey]]) | college = [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] (2017–2020) | highlights = * First-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] (2020) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2017 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2017]]) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2017) * [[Nike Hoop Summit]] (2017) }} '''Nicholas Richards''' (born November 29, 1997) is a Jamaican [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]]. ==High school career== [[File:20170329 MCDAAG Nicholas Richards on the fast break.jpg|thumb|left|Richards at the [[2017 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2017 McDonald's All-American Game]]]] Born and grew up in [[Kingston, Jamaica]],{{Cite web|url=https://davesjoint.net/2016/09/19/nick-richards-the-journey-from-jamaica-to-jersey/|title=Nick Richards: The Journey from Jamaica to Jersey|date=September 19, 2016|access-date=July 9, 2017}} Richards competed in soccer, volleyball and track and field before being discovered by Andre Ricketts, a [[New York City]] based basketball scout, in the summer of 2013 during a basketball camp in Jamaica. {{Cite web|url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2016/11/10/journey-jamaica-jersey-nick-richards-commits-kentucky/|title=After Journey from Jamaica to Jersey, Nick Richards Commits to Kentucky|last=Zagoria|first=Adam|date=November 10, 2016|website=Zagsblog|access-date=July 9, 2017}} Ricketts brought him to the US, where Richards attended [[St. Mary's High School (Manhasset, New York)|St. Mary's High School]] in [[Manhasset, New York]]. He transferred to [[The Patrick School]] in [[Hillside, New Jersey]] in 2014.{{Cite web|url=http://www.zagsblog.com/2014/10/23/big-man-nick-richards-with-kentucky-type-talent-transfers-to-the-patrick-school/|title=Big Man Nick Richards With 'Kentucky-Type Talent' Transfers to The Patrick School|last=Zagoria|first=Adam|date=October 23, 2014|website=Zagsblog|access-date=July 9, 2017}} He was ranked a five-star recruit in the class of 2017 (by [[ESPN]]) and committed to [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|the University of Kentucky]] in November 2016.{{Cite news|url=http://www.scout.com/college/basketball/recruiting/story/1726541-5-star-nick-richards-commits-to-kentucky|title=5-star Nick Richards commits to Kentucky|work=Scout.com|access-date=July 9, 2017|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161113151344/http://www.scout.com/college/basketball/recruiting/story/1726541-5-star-nick-richards-commits-to-kentucky|archive-date=November 13, 2016|url-status=dead}} He was UK’s first commit in the class of 2017 and chose Kentucky over [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]] and [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]]. Richards played in the [[2017 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]],{{Cite news|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2017/kentucky-signee-nick-richards-calls-becoming-mcdonalds-all-american-a-dream-come-true|title=Kentucky signee Nick Richards calls becoming McDonald's All American a dream come true|date=January 25, 2017|work=USA Today High School Sports|access-date=July 9, 2017|language=en-US}} pouring in two points, grabbing two rebounds and tallying two blocked shots in 14 minutes of action.{{Cite news|url=http://tucson.com/mcdonald-s-all-american-game-box-score/pdf_3a97a340-1506-11e7-9032-ff5c2217fb5e.html|title=2017 McDonald's All-American Game box score|work=Arizona Daily Star|access-date=July 6, 2017|language=en}} Participating in the 2017 [[Jordan Brand Classic]], he had ten points and three boards in 16 minutes of play.{{Cite web|url=http://jordanbrandclassic.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/04/2017-Jordan-Brand-Classic-National-Boys-Game.pdf|title=Official Basketball Box Score -- Game Totals -- Final Statistics East Team vs West Team|website=jordanbrandclassic.com|access-date=July 6, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170928010232/http://jordanbrandclassic.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/04/2017-Jordan-Brand-Classic-National-Boys-Game.pdf|archive-date=September 28, 2017|url-status=dead}} Richards was picked to play for the World Select Team at the 2017 [[Nike Hoop Summit]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.fiba.com/news/fiba-youth-stars-set-to-showcase-skills-at-nike-hoop-summit|title=FIBA youth stars set to showcase skills at Nike Hoop Summit|website=FIBA.basketball|language=en|access-date=July 9, 2017}} He saw 19:29 minutes of action during the game, scoring 12 points and grabbing three rebounds.{{Cite web|url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/media/pdfs/2017/17-hsum-box-scorepdf.aspx|title=Nike Hoop Summit Box Scores|website=usab.com|access-date=July 9, 2017}} ==College career== Richards had then-career-highs of 25 points and 15 rebounds on November 22, 2017, contributing to the Wildcats' 86–67 win over [[IPFW Mastodons basketball|IPFW]].{{cite news |title=No. 8 Kentucky finally has it easy against Fort Wayne, 86–67 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400987192 |accessdate=November 9, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 22, 2017}} He averaged 5.1 points and 4.4 rebounds per game as a freshman but saw his playing time decrease as the season went on.{{cite news |last1=Roberts |first1=Ben |title=Forget what you saw last season. There’s a new Nick Richards at Kentucky. |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article219452960.html |accessdate=November 9, 2019 |work=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]] |date=October 8, 2018}} Richards posted 3.9 points and 3.3 rebounds per game as a sophomore and led the team in blocks. Following the season he delared for the [[2019 NBA draft]] but opted to return to Kentucky.{{cite news |last1=Hale |first1=Jon |title=Nick Richards withdraws from NBA draft to return to Kentucky for junior season |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2019/05/28/kentucky-basketball-nick-richards-withdraws-nba-draft/3760187002/ |accessdate=November 9, 2019 |work=[[Louisville Courier-Journal]] |date=May 28, 2019}} On November 8, 2019, Richards scored 21 points and grabbed 10 rebounds as Kentucky defeated [[Eastern Kentucky Colonels men's basketball|Eastern Kentucky]] 91–49.{{cite news |title=No. 2 Kentucky easily handles Eastern Kentucky 91–49 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401169808 |accessdate=November 9, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 8, 2019}} He had 21 points, 12 rebounds and four blocks on January 4, 2020, in a 71–59 win over [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]].{{cite news |title=No. 17 Kentucky outlasts Missouri 71–59 in SEC opener |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166272 |accessdate=January 24, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=January 4, 2020}} Richards had 25 points including the two clinching free throws and 13 rebounds on January 25, in a 76–74 overtime win over [[Texas Tech Red Raiders men's basketball|Texas Tech]].{{cite news |title=No. 15 Kentucky pulls out 76-74 OT win at No. 18 Texas Tech |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401169716 |accessdate=January 27, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=January 25, 2020}} On February 4, Richards set a new career-high with 27 points on an 80–72 win over [[Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball|Mississippi State]].{{cite news |title=No. 15 Kentucky bounces back to beat Mississippi State 80–72 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166327 |accessdate=February 5, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 4, 2020}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Richards was named to the First Team All-SEC.{{cite press release|url=https://www.secsports.com/article/28877731/sec-announces-2020-men-basketball-awards |title=SEC announces 2020 Men's Basketball Awards |publisher=Southeastern Conference |date=March 10, 2020 |accessdate=March 10, 2020}} He averaged 14 points, 7.8 rebounds, and 2.1 blocks per game.{{cite news |last1=Fisher |first1=Chris |title=Four Wildcats projected among ESPN's top 60 NBA Draft prospects |url=https://247sports.com/college/kentucky/LongFormArticle/Four-Kentucky-Wildcats-projected-among-ESPNs-top-60-NBA-Draft-prospects-145082340/#145082340_2 |accessdate=March 18, 2020 |work=247 Sports |date=March 16, 2020}} Following the season, Richards declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last1=Phillips |first1=Scott |title=Nick Richards leaving Kentucky for 2020 NBA draft |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2020/04/14/nick-richards/ |accessdate=April 14, 2020 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=April 14, 2020}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}}
